A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PARC framework and PERL dataset. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original premise-identification and error-identification experiments on PERL, including model comparisons in Tables 1–10 and manual checks of generated annotations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments, numerical results, and annotation checks in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain aggregative and dyadic premise mapping, premise-conditioned verification, and graph traversal for accumulation-error detection. No algorithm component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate premise identification and error identification using GSM8K, MATH, Orca-Math, and MetaMathQA-derived PERL examples, retaining positive, negative, and synthetic-negative coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same model lineups and comparisons: Full Context versus Model Premises, oracle versus model-generated premises, and aggregative versus dyadic mapping.

E3.justification: Sampling, splits, annotation procedures, model configurations, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Both retain zero-shot evaluation, temperature-zero generation, premise precision/recall/F1, and the same averaging procedure for error-identification accuracy.

E4.justification: The mapping comparison, oracle-premise ablation, error-type breakdown, synthetic-versus-natural negative analysis, and Figure 2 case study are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Reporting and aggregation practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–10 and the illustrated findings are unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports Llama 3.1 70B GSM8K average accuracy of 71.37 under Full Context and 81.92 under Model Premises in both versions.

T1.justification: The premise verifiability and minimality conditions, reasoning-chain equations, dyadic mapping definition, and formal error categories remain unchanged. No mathematical result, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about reliable premise identification, improved error detection, accumulation errors, and PERL. The abstract's 90% recall and 6–16 percentage-point improvement claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations concerning model scale, distractors, correct-step accuracy tradeoffs, and overly optimistic evaluation using synthetic negatives. The human-oversight caveat in Section 7 is unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 and the annotation/evaluation prompts retain the same technical information. The new acknowledgment identifies funding for Azure access already documented in A.1; it adds no implementation settings, reproduction instructions, or code/data availability information.

R1.justification: The cited works and reference entries are unchanged after matching text across page breaks. Section 2 and the introduction retain the same positioning relative to reasoning evaluators and verifiers.

P1.justification: v4 adds Section 8 acknowledging Microsoft AFMR support, replaces the anonymous correspondence placeholder with Sagnik Mukherjee's contact information, and adjusts title capitalization and author markers. Scientific prose and narrative organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment causes limited reflow of references and appendix text, including splitting the A.3 JSON template across pages 13–14. Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–16 retain their content, structure, and visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v4 adds funding transparency and usable correspondence information, providing slight administrative polish. The scientific argument, empirical evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility instructions remain unchanged, while appendix text merely reflows. These limited edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
